3c.ruling: final-answer error (algorithm, inverted comparison and bound)
3c.note: I ran the official loop literally (1-indexed, 'while j<m and flag'; equal -> both ++; 'else if A2[j] > A1[i]' -> flag=false; else j++). It is wrong on 1444 of 3000 random inputs. Three defects: (1) comparison inverted: when A2[j] > A1[i] the right move is i++ (T1 element too small), and failure is when A2[j] < A1[i] (the T2 key was skipped); (2) the last branch advances j instead of i; (3) 'j<m' should be 'j<=m' (1-indexed), so for m=1 the loop never runs and the answer is always 'yes' (official gives yes for T1={1,2,3}, T2={5}); also i must be bounded by n. Counter-examples: T1={2,5},T2={8} -> official yes, correct no; T1={2,6,7,9},T2={6,9} -> official no, correct yes. Correct answer: inorder both to sorted arrays; i=j=1; while i<=n and j<=m: if A1[i]=A2[j] then i++,j++; elif A1[i]<A2[j] then i++; else return no; return (j>m). Time Theta(n) (n+m). Efficiency note: since m<=n, searching each T2 key in T1 costs O(m log n), better when m << n/log n; official's Theta(n) is not strictly 'most efficient' (needs a הערה or accept O(min(n, m log n))). Stored solution reproduces the defective loop verbatim; step 2 (text accept Theta(n)/O(n)) matches the official but would reject O(m log n).

4a.note: Official 'true' is correct only as a worst-case statement: the key moves up (<= r swaps) or down (<= m-r swaps), never both, and a node at A[2^r] has depth r and subtree height m-r, so at most max{r,m-r} swaps, attained for extreme new keys. Read literally ('exactly max{r,m-r} swaps are required for a given change') it is false (unchanged or slightly changed key needs 0). Needs a הערה ('at most / worst case'), and the stored solution should state the depth r and height m-r argument; it currently gives only 'heapify up or down'.

4b.note: True: sorted input costs n-1 comparisons (each element vs its left neighbour) and every leaf needs >= n-1 (comparison graph must be connected). Simulation of insertion sort over all permutations n=2..7: min leaf depth = n-1, max = n(n-1)/2. BUT the official reasoning is wrong: 'a minimum element is swapped against all elements to its left' describes the MAXIMUM depth, not the minimum. Key agrees, explanation does not.
4b.correctExplanation: Sorted input: element i is compared only with element i-1, total n-1; any leaf needs at least n-1 comparisons since otherwise two comparison-components remain and the order of the whole input is undetermined.
